articles.title: Dunas em Barroquinha: areia bloqueia CE-187 e afeta Bitupitá | G1
articles.standfirst: A obstrução ocorre há cerca de 45 dias em um trecho de 250 metros da CE-187. A prefeitura atua com máquinas para tentar liberar a via e amenizar transtornos.
articles.summary: A obstrução ocorre há cerca de 45 dias em um trecho de 250 metros da CE-187. A prefeitura atua com máquinas para tentar liberar a via e amenizar transtornos.
articles.body:
Moradores de Bitupitá, distrito de Barroquinha , no interior do Ceará, relatam dificuldades para transitar após o avanço de dunas sobre um trecho da CE-187 . A estrada liga a sede do município à localidade litorânea de seis mil habitantes, conhecida pelo turismo e pela pesca.

Vídeos gravados por moradores mostram a rodovia coberta pela areia. Alguns carros e motos chegam a atolar no local. Segundo relatos ouvidos pelo g1 , além do desafio para percorrer a via, o bloqueio também estaria dificultando a chegada de suprimentos básicos, como água e alimentos, o que preocupa a população.

Em entrevista ao g1 , o prefeito de Barroquinha, Jaime Veras, afirmou que as dunas avançam sobre um trecho de aproximadamente 250 metros. Segundo ele, a situação se arrasta há cerca de 45 dias, mas, nesta semana, a circulação de veículos de grande porte voltou a ser possível.

➡️ A prefeitura informou também que equipes trabalham na retirada da areia com o auxílio de máquinas . Ainda conforme Jaime, a gestão municipal busca soluções para garantir o tráfego de moradores, visitantes e caminhões que abastecem a região, além de medidas para resolver a situação de forma definitiva (entenda mais abaixo).

Dunas cobrem pista que dá acesso a comunidade pesqueira no litoral cearense e isola população. — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Moradores relatam prejuízos e isolamento

O empresário Arimateia de Carvalho , dono de uma pousada e de um restaurante em Bitupitá, afirma que a dificuldade de deslocamento tem afetado os negócios. No último fim de semana, nos dias 7 e 8 de novembro, ele não recebeu hóspedes. O caminhão responsável por levar mercadorias para repor o estoque dos estabelecimentos também não conseguiu chegar ao distrito.

“Isso é um problema antigo. Só que eles só resolvem mexer quando [as dunas] estão tomando a estrada. Quando chega o período de inverno, que o morro para, que não tem vento, eles deixam aí. Quando chega esse período [de mais ventos], ficamos isolados, sem entrar mercadoria no lugar ou caminhão grande. É o maior problema aqui pra gente de Bitupitá.”

A pedido do g1 , o empresário gravou um vídeo tentando atravessar o trecho da CE-187 de carro, na última quarta-feira (11). Trabalhadores e uma retroescavadeira atuam no local para retirar a areia, mas enfrentam dificuldade.

Pedestres e motociclistas também se arriscam pelo caminho de terra para chegar ao outro lado. Em meio à areia, poucas casas ainda se destacam. Segundo Arimateia, estudantes também vêm sendo prejudicados, porque o ônibus escolar não consegue passar no trecho. Os alunos fazem o percurso em vans.

“Todo ano acontece algo parecido, só que dessa vez foi pior. E em uma emergência com alguém doente ou passando mal? É um problema sério que está afetando não só a Bitupitá, mas também uma praia vizinha, que é Curimãs. São as duas populações que estão sendo muito prejudicadas”, lamentou.

O empresário defende que a prefeitura dialogue com a comunidade de Bitupitá sobre medidas permanentes para resolver o problema. Segundo ele, no entanto, isso ainda não ocorreu.

Duna toma estrada que dá acesso a distrito da cidade de Barroquinha, no litoral cearense — Foto: Reprodução

“Eles nunca fizeram reunião com a gente, eles nunca chamaram a gente pra audiência na Câmara de Vereadores, nem Prefeitura, nada. Simplesmente a gente fica aqui sem saber. É uma situação complicada.”

Outra moradora do distrito, a auxiliar administrativa Verônica Maria Veras , conta que costumava caminhar quase todos os dias perto da estrada, hábito que interrompeu nas últimas semanas. Ela relata dificuldade para transitar a pé e lembra de situações que evidenciam os transtornos provocados pelo avanço da areia.

“Um colega faleceu no hospital [localizado na sede]. Estava previsto para o corpo chegar em Bitupitá às 18h, mas foi chegar 22h, porque um carro estava atolado na estrada e o carro da funerária não conseguia passar”, lamentou.

Dunas cobrem pista em cidade do Ceará. — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

O pesquisador Eduardo Lacerda Barros, especialista em geologia e geomorfologia costeira e oceânica, estuda a região de Bitupitá há alguns anos. Em 2021, ele colaborou no artigo "Migração de dunas e o processo de soterramento no litoral de Barroquinha, Ceará, Brasil" .

Segundo Eduardo, o vento leva a areia pela rampa da duna e a despeja pelo outro lado, que é íngreme. "Assim, a duna inteira avança, grão a grão" , resume o pesquisador.

No estudo realizado por Eduardo Lacerda, Renan Gonçalves, Andréa de Sousa, João Rafael Muniz e Hermógenes Henrique, as dunas mais ativas de Barroquinha avançaram em média de 12 a 19 metros por ano, ou seja, entre um e um metro e meio por mês.

Praia de Curimãs, localidade de Bitupitá — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Barroquinha

“Nas mais rápidas, isso equivale ao comprimento de um campo de futebol a cada cinco ou seis anos. Quando essa frente íngreme alcança a estrada, a pista passa de livre a coberta em pouco tempo, e daí vem a sensação de algo repentino. Neste período do ano a força é maior porque estamos na estação seca: os ventos de leste são mais intensos, não chove e a areia está seca e solta, que é a combinação ideal para ela ser transportada."

O pesquisador reforça que o problema surgiu porque a estrada foi construída atravessando o caminho natural por onde essas dunas se deslocam . Naquela região, elas encontram os fatores ideais para crescer: muita areia disponível vinda das praias, vento forte e constante, e uma planície ampla por onde essa areia corre livremente.

"A duna não escolheu a estrada. O encontro era uma questão de tempo. Na região de Venâncio está o maior campo de dunas que estudamos, e ele continua recebendo areia de dunas mais novas que vêm de trás. Além disso, obstáculos no caminho, como vegetação e construções, fazem a areia se acumular, e a duna cresce ainda mais", acrescenta o pesquisador.

Orla de Bitupitá. — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Barroquinha

A região onde as dunas avançam sobre a estrada integra a Área de Proteção Ambiental do Delta do Parnaíba, gerida pelo Instituto Chico Mendes de Conservação da Biodiversidade (ICMBio), mas a gestão municipal adota medidas paliativas para amenizar a situação.

O prefeito de Barroquinha, Jaime Veras, disse ao g1 que estuda formas de resolver a situação de maneira permanente, para além da retirada da areia acumulada sobre a via.

Ele explicou que as dunas avançam sobre um trecho de aproximadamente 250 metros da estrada. O problema ocorre há cerca de 45 dias, mas foi amenizado na última semana, quando voltou a ser possível a circulação de veículos de grande porte.

“Neste momento, estamos com dois carros-pipa molhando a areia no trecho por onde os carros estão passando, para melhorar o trânsito. Hoje, mesmo com o maquinário no local, não temos condições de fazer a retirada da areia porque, quando coloca a concha da máquina, outra parte desaba. O que estamos aguardando de verdade é o início do inverno, para fazer a retirada com mais segurança”, explicou o prefeito.

Jaime Veras também informou que cerca de 10 equipamentos, além de uma equipe especializada, atuam no local para amenizar os transtornos . Sobre a dificuldade na chegada de suprimentos básicos, ele afirmou que a via está liberada para caminhões com cargas.

“A Prefeitura, desde que assumimos em 2021, vem fazendo a manutenção e a retirada da areia. Como é uma rodovia estadual, estivemos com o pessoal do Ibama, da Semace e da UFC para fazer um estudo. Em 2022, fomos até a SOP [Superintendência de Obras Públicas], cobramos a responsabilidade do órgão também, sem nos omitir da nossa parte.”

➡️ Só em Bitupitá, moram cerca de 6 mil pessoas, o que representa aproximadamente 41% da população de Barroquinha. Segundo o Censo 2022 do Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE), o município tem 14.567 habitantes.

Ainda de acordo com Jaime Veras, a prefeitura estuda medidas para resolver o problema de forma definitiva. As duas principais possibilidades são:

construir uma estrada alternativa para ligar a sede de Barroquinha a Bitupitá e outras localidades;

“Como é uma rodovia estadual, a SOP apresentou algumas alternativas. Um setor de engenharia do órgão esteve na região estudando a possibilidade de uma rodovia pela orla. Nós temos 22 quilômetros de litoral. E eu também sugeri a ideia de uma ponte, mas não sei se eles vão avaliar. Não se sabe o custo, mas são as duas únicas opções”, disse o prefeito.

O prefeito acrescentou que sua maior preocupação é com o deslocamento da população entre as localidades, especialmente em situações de urgência, como a passagem de ambulâncias. Ainda em novembro, segundo ele, a gestão municipal deve se reunir com o Governo do Estado para acelerar a discussão sobre uma rota alternativa.

“Ali é, como se diz aqui, enxugar gelo. Vamos retirar a areia no inverno para liberar a pista. Acredito que vamos levar mais de dois meses, intensificando os serviços. E sabendo que, quando chegar o verão, vamos voltar a lutar contra os ventos que jogam areia sobre o asfalto”, concluiu Veras.

Barroquinha é conhecida pelas praias e por ser uma região de pesca. — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Barroquinha

Segundo o pesquisador Eduardo Lacerda, remover a areia da pista não resolve o problema por completo, porque esse material “é só a frente da duna”. Ou seja, o corpo da duna continua atrás, e a praia segue fornecendo areia nova.

“Retirar a areia da estrada é como enxugar o chão com a torneira aberta: alivia a emergência, mas o fluxo continua, a areia volta e o serviço precisa ser repetido”, afirmou.

Para Eduardo, a palavra-chave é “convivência” . Ele lista algumas formas de enfrentar o problema:

monitorar o avanço das dunas e mapear o que está em risco;

não permitir novas construções e loteamentos no caminho natural das dunas;

instalar cercas para reter a areia e fazer o plantio de vegetação nativa apenas em trechos críticos, sem fixar todo o campo de dunas;

quando a remoção for necessária, destinar a areia a um local definido tecnicamente;

envolver o ICMBio, o estado e o município nas intervenções, já que a área está dentro de uma APA.

“A solução mais duradoura é retirar a infraestrutura do caminho das dunas, desde que o novo traçado seja estudado para não cruzar outro campo de dunas ativo. Já se fala publicamente em um desvio da rodovia, e esse caminho faz sentido do ponto de vista técnico. Nada disso funciona sem que os moradores entendam como as dunas se movem e participem das decisões ”, reforçou o especialista.

O g1 entrou em contato com o ICMBio para entender se há algum projeto em análise para intervenções que evitem o soterramento recorrente da via e resolvam de forma definitiva a questão. Em nota, o instituto disse:

"A retirada das dunas que cobrem a rodovia é questão de utilidade pública. Essa atividade cabe ao poder municipal. Não há restrições impostas pelo Instituto Chico Mendes (ICMBio/MMA)".

articles.title: Uber Moto no RJ: Mulheres são 60% dos usuários e lideram viagens | G1
articles.standfirst: Fluxo de corridas aumenta nos horários de entrada e saída do trabalho. Dados foram divulgados pela Uber na quinta-feira (12), durante um evento no Rio de Janeiro.
articles.summary: O Uber Moto no Rio de Janeiro lidera viagens no país com 60% de público feminino, motivando a criação de novas ferramentas de segurança para as passageiras.
articles.body:
Para muitos trabalhadores, chegar ao emprego depende não somente de pegar um ônibus, trem ou metrô. Em trajetos nos quais o transporte público não chega, em regiões com poucas opções de circulação ou em horários com oferta reduzida/ lotação de coletivos, o mototáxi e o motoUber se tornaram uma alternativa para viabilizar o deslocamento diário.

No Rio de Janeiro, cidade que concentra o maior volume de viagens de Uber Moto no Brasil, os dados da empresa apontam que a modalidade está incorporada à rotina de deslocamento dos passageiros na "hora do rush".

A análise dos horários também indica uma relação direta com a jornada de trabalho. Os maiores volumes de viagens acontecem entre 7h e 8h, pela manhã, e entre 17h e 18h, no fim da tarde, períodos que coincidem com os horários tradicionais de entrada e saída do expediente.

Segundo Silvia Penna, diretora-geral da Uber no Brasil, 60% dos usuários de Uber Moto são mulheres.

Outro dado apresentado pela empresa mostra que uma parcela significativa das viagens acontece de ou para estações de transporte público, como metrô, trem e ônibus. O serviço funciona, nesses casos, como uma conexão entre a casa ou o destino final e os principais meios de transporte coletivo.

“Tem uma porção de viagens significativa ali da primeira e última perna, integrando de forma complementar ao transporte público e já entrando na rotina do dia a dia dos cariocas”, afirmou Silvia Penna.

A personal trainer Joice Vilares tem dois filhos pequenos, mora no Méier, na Zona Norte do Rio, e trabalha em uma academia no Leblon, na Zona Sul. Segundo ela, a logística de deixar os filhos no colégio e seguir para o trabalho a tempo de chegar no horário certo só é possível graças à opção da viagem de moto por aplicativo.

"Pego motouber todos os dias. Se eu não fosse de moto, não conseguiria chegar no horário certo no trabalho, pois tenho que deixar meus filhos na escola e ainda cruzar a cidade. Tenho medo de acidentes, mas nunca aconteceu nada comigo. Procuro confiar porque essa é minha única opção", comenta Joice.

Matheus Costa, gerente de produtos, mora em Niterói e trabalha no Jardim Botânico. Ele faz viagens de moto de aplicativo para chegar ao ponto de ônibus no Centro de Niterói, em seguida, pega um coletivo para a Zona Sul.

Ele alega que perto de onde mora não tem ônibus com facilidade para fazer essa conexão.

"Para eu pegar um ônibus até o outro ônibus, preciso andar mais de meia hora. Só esse tempo, já impacta consideravelmente o tempo total de viagem até o trabalho. Quando uso a moto por aplicativo, o tempo total fica em 1 hora e 20 minutos. Quando pego dois ônibus, a viagem chega a 3 horas no total", relava Matheus.

Veja reportagens da série 'Epidemia das motos':

Empresa anuncia novas ferramentas de segurança

Os dados sobre o perfil dos usuários e os horários de utilização foram apresentados durante um evento da Uber no Rio de Janeiro, voltado à inovação em segurança para a modalidade.

Na ocasião, a empresa também divulgou resultados de iniciativas de prevenção de acidentes para os motociclistas e passageiros da Uber Moto. Segundo Silvia Penna, desde a implementação de alertas de direção, os relatos de comportamentos perigosos ao volante caíram 20%.

Uma reportagem do RJ2 mostrou que acidentes envolvendo motociclistas fazem cerca de 140 vítimas por dia no estado. No entanto, de acordo com a Uber, os acidentes não se refletem nos números da plataforma, relacionados ao transporte com passageiros.

A diretora-geral afirmou ainda que em menos de 0,003% das viagens de moto há registros de relatos de acidentes viários na plataforma. Segundo a diretora, a taxa de viagens seguras de moto na plataforma representa 99,997% em todo o país, sem nenhum tipo de incidente envolvendo segurança viária.

Entre as ferramentas utilizadas pela empresa estão alertas sonoros e visuais sobre excesso de velocidade, verificação do uso de capacete por meio de selfies e conteúdos educativos voltados a motoristas e passageiros. A Uber também utiliza dados de telemetria para identificar padrões de direção dos condutores.

Durante o evento, foram anunciadas novas funcionalidades para a modalidade. Uma delas conecta usuários que estão fazendo suas primeiras viagens de Uber Moto a motociclistas mais experientes, para auxiliar na experiência inicial.

Foto para identificar o passageiro em locais movimentados

Outra novidade é um sistema de preferências que permite ao passageiro indicar características desejadas para a condução, como uma viagem mais suave. A plataforma também passou a disponibilizar a foto do passageiro ao motorista, com o objetivo de facilitar a identificação nos pontos de embarque e desembarque, especialmente em locais movimentados, como estações de transporte público.

A empresa anunciou ainda um projeto-piloto no Rio de Janeiro de um botão Bluetooth que permite ao motociclista aceitar ou rejeitar viagens sem precisar tocar na tela do celular.

Segundo a Uber, as iniciativas fazem parte de uma estratégia de prevenção de riscos que envolve parcerias com organizações especializadas em segurança viária e produção de conteúdo educativo.

articles.title: Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar seeks 9th Schedule SC-ST quota cover
articles.summary: BENGALURU: Chief minister D K Shivakumar has written to PM Narendra Modi, urging him to bring about a constitutional amendment to include Karnataka
articles.body: BENGALURU: Chief minister D K Shivakumar has written to PM Narendra Modi, urging him to bring about a constitutional amendment to include Karnataka Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Act, 2022, in Ninth Schedule of the Constitution, thereby protecting its provision of reservations for SCs and STs in education and public employment.The law raised reservation for SCs from 15% to 17% and for STs from 3% to 7%, taking the overall quota to 56% in the state. It followed recommendations by a commission headed by retired Karnataka high court judge Justice H N Nagamohan Das.On Oct 12, 2026, HC struck down the enhanced reservation provisions, ruling that the aggregate quota exceeded the 50% ceiling. Clarifying govt’s position, Shivakumar said the issues flagged by HC called for a constitutional solution and shouldn’t result in abandon-ing SC-ST communities’ aspirations for educational and employment opportunities.Shivakumar said Karnataka’s proposal predated high court verdict, having been submitted to Union govt on March 23, 2023.CM: K’taka’s plea must get same attention as TN’s caseCiting Tamil Nadu’s 69% reservation framework, which was included in the Ninth Schedule through the Constitution (76th Amendment) Act, 1994, he wrote: “If Parliament could act to protect a reservation framework of 69% in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka’s request for 56% reservation, founded on the recommendations of a judicial commission, deserves no less constitutional attention.”The legislative assembly passed a resolution seeking Ninth Schedule protection on Dec 18, 2025, while former chief minister Siddaramaiah reiterated the demand in a letter to Modi on April 16, 2026.In a Lok Sabha reply on July 25, 2026, the Union govt acknowledged receiving the proposal, but said Ninth Schedule inclusion was not appropriate while the matter was pending before the court.Following the high court verdict, Shivakumar urged the Centre not to defer consideration on account of the ongoing appellate proceedings.He sought consultations with the National Commissions for SCs and STs and a time-bound examination by the ministries of law and justice, social justice and empowerment, tribal affairs, and home affairs.Karnataka, he said, was ready to provide empirical material and address the constitutional and procedural issues identified by the court.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bengaluru | Silver Rate in Bengaluru | Bank Holidays in Bengaluru | Public Holidays in Bengaluru | Bengaluru AQI | Weather in Bengaluru | Petrol Price in Bengaluru | Diesel Price in Bengaluru | CNG Price in Bengaluru | LPG Price in BengaluruStay updated with the latest Bengaluru news. articles.title: Saudi-led coalition intercepts suspected Houthi missiles and drones
articles.summary: Fighting escalates in Yemen’s Marib and al-Jawf, as UN agency says more than 340,000 Yemenis displaced since August.
articles.body:
Saudi-led coalition forces fighting Yemen’s Houthis have said they intercepted two missiles and five drones targeting different parts of the country, allegedly launched by the Iran-backed rebel group.

“Air defences intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthi terrorist militia towards Riyadh,” Turki al-Maliki, the Saudi-led coalition spokesperson, said in a post on X early on Sunday.

He said the coalition forces also shot down three drones in Saudi Arabia’s Eastern region on Sunday.

Earlier on Saturday, al-Maliki said two suspected Houthi drones “were intercepted and destroyed” in the Riyadh and southern regions.

Meanwhile, the Houthis, an armed group also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God), claimed to have shot down an armed Saudi coalition reconnaissance aircraft carrying out “hostile operations in the airspace of al-Jawf”.

In a post on X, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the Iran-aligned group was able to “repel a number of Saudi military formations using several Yemeni-made surface-to-air missiles” and that it was the fifth aircraft the Houthis had shot down since the escalation began.

At least 26 people have been killed in suspected Houthi drone and missile attacks in Saudi Arabia since September 23, according to the kingdom’s authorities.

The Houthis have repeatedly targeted Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport, as well as the East-West pipeline and oil infrastructure in eastern and southern Saudi Arabia.

The interceptions come as the Saudi-led forces supporting Yemen’s internationally recognised government also said they intercepted several drones launched towards the Yemeni city of Marib.

Yemeni army spokesman Colonel Majid al-Nuzaili said government forces had made gains against the Houthis during heavy fighting in the al-Hazm and Madghal districts of al-Jawf, as fighting intensified in Marib.

Al-Nuzaili said 321 Houthi leaders had been killed or wounded in 723 targeted operations by Saudi-backed forces in the Taiz, Lahij, Marib and al-Jawf governorates, and that 117 military vehicles used by the Iran-allied rebel group had been destroyed.

The coalition carried out at least 37 air strikes and 56 drone attacks, as well as 541 artillery strikes.

Houthi spokesman Saree said the Saudi-led coalition had launched 72 air strikes against the Houthis in the Saada, Taiz, Lahij and al-Jawf governorates over the past 24 hours.

He said the Houthis targeted Yemen’s Saudi-backed forces in the Kharaz area of the Lahij governorate with ballistic missiles.

Media outlets affiliated with the Houthis reported that two women and two children were injured as a result of artillery shelling by Saudi-backed forces in a residential neighbourhood of the Shuaub district in Sanaa, Yemen’s capital controlled by the Houthis.

More than 340,000 people have been displaced as a result of fighting in Yemen since August, according to the International Organization for Migration.

As the fight between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis escalated, the US Embassy in Riyadh issued a nationwide security alert on Saturday urging Americans in the kingdom to exercise “heightened vigilance”, citing an increased threat of Houthi attacks.

The embassy said Houthi attacks on airports and other critical infrastructure in Saudi Arabia had “caused civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions”, warning that hostilities could spread “rapidly”.

“Please take extreme caution if you choose to use airports in Saudi Arabia,” it said.

articles.title: 'My home for many years': Lalit Modi gets British citizenship 16 years after leaving India
articles.summary: Former Indian Premier League (IPL) chairman Lalit Modi has acquired British citizenship, announcing the development at an address to the Oxford Union,
articles.body: Former Indian Premier League (IPL) chairman Lalit Modi has acquired British citizenship, announcing the development at an address to the Oxford Union, nearly 16 years after leaving India amid allegations of financial irregularities linked to his tenure as the cricket league's chief.Lalit, who said he formally became a British citizen on September 15, shared the news late Saturday, describing it as a proud and deeply personal milestone. He said he celebrated the occasion with family and friends at a citizenship ceremony in the United Kingdom, where he has lived for several years.In a post on X, the IPL founder said the UK had been his home for many years and that he had developed a deep appreciation for its people, institutions, traditions and values. "The United Kingdom has been my home for many years. It is a country I have come to admire and appreciate deeply — its people, institutions, traditions and values. Becoming British is a privilege and a responsibility that I embrace with pride, gratitude and a genuine sense of belonging," he wrote.He also thanked the organisation for providing an opportunity to share the news, adding that announcing it on the occasion of King Charles III's birthday made the moment particularly special. "My life's journey has been shaped by different cultures and experiences, and I look forward to continuing to contribute positively to the country I proudly call home," he added.Modi left India in 2010 following his removal as IPL chairman by the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI). He has since faced allegations of financial irregularities during his tenure, including bid-rigging, money laundering and violations of the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA).The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has investigated alleged financial irregularities and unauthorised fund transfers linked to the IPL. Indian authorities have also pursued extradition-related processes.Modi, however, has repeatedly rejected the description of himself as a fugitive, arguing that he has never been convicted of a crime.In an interview with news agency ANI earlier this year, he dismissed the label as media sensationalism and denied that he had been evading Indian authorities since leaving the country. "I'm not running at all. I'm going all over the world. If I was running, you would be picking me up somewhere or the other. The Indian government has a long arm," he had said.He also questioned why, despite years of investigations, he had not been brought before a court. "Not a single case against me has been registered. If I have been so bad, and everybody says I've been so bad, OK, please, guys, go out and prosecute me," he told ANI.On the possibility of returning to India to contest the allegations, Modi said he no longer felt the need to prove himself. He also alleged that political opponents had repeatedly targeted him.Despite his assertions, investigations linked to his tenure as IPL chairman remain a part of the legal and regulatory scrutiny surrounding him.You use AI every day. articles.title: New York Democratic Socialists urge Ocasio-Cortez to run for US president
articles.summary: Delegates at NYC-DSA convention pass resolution formally calling on Congresswoman AOC to run in 2028 presidential race.
articles.body:
The New York City chapter of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) has voted to urge Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez to run for United States president in 2028, a move that could serve as an early bellwether for the Democratic Party’s direction in the presidential race.

The resolution passed 291 to 123 at the chapter’s convention on Saturday. While it is not a formal endorsement by the DSA, it commits the New York City chapter to encouraging a presidential bid and building the groundwork for a potential campaign.

“If the US can elect Trump, I think we can elect Democratic Socialists,” Gustavo Gordillo, NYC-DSA co-chair, told Al Jazeera, referring to President Donald Trump.

The convention was held following a strong showing by DSA-endorsed candidates in the midterm elections. A record eight DSA-endorsed candidates were elected to federal office and will hold congressional seats in January.

Ocasio-Cortez, popularly known as AOC, is a longtime member of NYC-DSA, the chapter covering her home city. The New York City branch, which has about 15,000 members, has become one of the movement’s most influential. It endorsed Mayor Zohran Mamdani last year and has backed Ocasio-Cortez in all five of her congressional general elections since 2018.

That electoral influence has given the chapter a prominent voice in shaping the direction of progressive politics in the US.

“Now that we have put a mayor into City Hall and we’ve elected three socialists in the city, I think regardless of how a politician feels about DSA personally, they’re definitely looking at what we say and how we’re moving,” NYC-DSA co-chair Grace Mausser said. “We are one of the biggest political actors in the city, in the state, and the country, frankly.”

Ocasio-Cortez, a Democrat representing New York’s 14th congressional district, rose to national prominence in 2018 after defeating a 10-term incumbent in a congressional primary. A prominent Democratic Socialist, she has advocated for policies including universal healthcare, tuition-free public college and labour protections.

The chapter has yet to finalise a national presidential platform. Mausser said it would be built around issues members encounter when speaking with voters.

“The top issues at the doors that we encounter are housing, healthcare, childcare – the hallmarks of affordability,” Mausser said. “Those would all become the core of a federal platform.”

The resolution text says the campaign would provide an opportunity for “continued crafting of a platform that engages the working class”. It also identifies public housing, stopping the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agency, labour organising and “the anti-war and pro-Palestine movements” as priorities.

The NYC-DSA vote adds to mounting efforts on the left to persuade Ocasio-Cortez to enter the 2028 presidential race, following a debate within the national DSA over her possible endorsement and the launch of an independent campaign urging her to run, called “Ready for AOC”.

Ocasio-Cortez has previously she will decide on her political future after the midterm elections, leaving open the possibility of a 2028 presidential bid or a challenge for a US Senate seat.

articles.title: Masked dirt bike riders swarm SUV in brazen NYC street attack, sparking police crackdown
articles.summary: Video captures masked dirt bike riders swarming and attacking an SUV on a busy Staten Island street as the NYPD warns that arrests are near.
articles.body: New York City officials are warning a group of masked dirt bike riders that arrests could be imminent after video captured a chaotic confrontation in which several riders surrounded and attacked a vehicle on a busy Staten Island street. The crackdown follows a Wednesday incident on Richmond Avenue in Staten Island's Bulls Head neighborhood, where video showed several masked riders swarming a white SUV stopped at a traffic light. In the video obtained by Fox News Digital, several individuals appeared to kick and strike the vehicle, while another appeared to throw an object at it. As the driver attempted to leave, the SUV appeared to run over a dirt bike that had been positioned in front of the vehicle. WATCH: E-BIKE TEEN TAKEOVER SWARMS DOWNTOWN CITY STREETS BLOCKING TRAFFIC, LEADING TO CHARGES During a news conference Thursday, NYPD Assistant Chief John Buttacavoli warned those involved that police were gathering intelligence and working to identify the suspects. "We know who you are, and you will be getting a knock on your door very soon," Buttacavoli said, emphasizing that the behavior had escalated from a quality-of-life concern into criminal activity. "It stops here. We're taking action," he added. Staten Island District Attorney Michael McMahon also condemned the riders, accusing them of intimidating motorists and putting innocent people at risk. VIDEO SHOWS BRIDGE TURN INTO BURNOUT BONANZA IN STUNT-HAPPY TAKEOVER – POLICE SWOOP IN TO CUFF ROAD REBELS "Like a plague of locusts, they descend upon drivers who are just going about their business here on Staten Island," McMahon said. "They're jackals, they're teenage terrorists, and it's not going to be tolerated here in our borough." McMahon called the behavior "simply outrageous," adding that no one had been seriously injured, based on the information available to officials. Wednesday's incident was part of a broader pattern of dangerous behavior involving motorized bikes, according to Staten Island Borough President Vito Fossella. Fossella described the riders as a "bunch of punks who are literally terrorizing drivers" as motorists went about their daily routines. "Enough. This game is over," Fossella said. The borough president also warned parents that their children were putting innocent motorists at risk. CITIES FEARING HALLOWEEN MAYHEM PUT TEENS ON NOTICE, ANNOUNCE CURFEWS AND CRACKDOWNS AFTER VIOLENT TAKEOVERS "Your kid is terrorizing innocent people when they're just going about their business. It's wrong, and it needs to stop," Fossella said. McMahon warned that parents could face legal or financial consequences if their children use illegal motorized vehicles to intimidate or injure others, including potential civil liability if someone is hurt. "Parents also must take responsibility for their children," McMahon's office said in a separate statement. Police have assembled a task force to address the problem and will continue confiscating illegally operated motorized bikes, according to Buttacavoli. He said officers had already identified several individuals and seized numerous bikes this year. GRINNING SUSPECT CUFFED AFTER ALLEGED FIERY STREET TAKEOVER, DRAG RACE CAUGHT ON CAMERA The NYPD also reminded residents that certain motorized vehicles must be registered, insured and operated by licensed drivers. State Assemblyman Mike Reilly, R-Staten Island, said he plans to introduce legislation in January that would hold parents financially responsible for minors caught recklessly operating certain motorized vehicles, according to the New York Post. The proposal would impose fines ranging from $250 to $1,500, the paper reported. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The incident remains under investigation, and no arrests have been announced.

articles.title: Arch Manning turns Death Valley into LSU’s funeral as Texas buries Lane Kiffin’s CFP hopes
articles.summary: Lane Kiffin's $40 million LSU roster watched Arch Manning deliver a late touchdown pass to Raleek Brown that ended the Tigers' playoff dreams.
articles.body: BATON ROUGE, La. — Turns out, the Texas Longhorns had one last drive left in them, on a night when nothing was going Arch Manning's way. What we witnessed on Saturday night inside Tiger Stadium will be remembered for quite some time, by both Texas and LSU fans. What started as a party for the Tiger faithful turned into a funeral for the LSU 2026 season that will leave folks in Louisiana wondering how they could give this one away to the Longhorns. LSU HEAD COACH LANE KIFFIN IS MAKING THE SAME MISTAKE HIS PREDECESSOR DID, WILL HE SUFFER THE SAME FATE? The pressure entering this one was heavy on both sides. Texas could not afford another loss and feel totally safe in making the postseason, while a fourth loss for LSU would put an end to their CFP hopes, even if they were already hanging by a thread. Was there some hesitation among LSU fans to get overly excited about this one? If you were wondering why, the final drive of this game all but proved their point that Lane Kiffin is the same guy who could not win the big game at Ole Miss, and now as head coach of the Tigers. Maybe that's because Sam Leavitt had three interceptions through three quarters tonight, and it's hard to trust this LSU offense at times. It wasn’t if the other side was any better though, with Arch Manning throwing three of his own. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE It had to end this way for the Tigers, at the hands of Louisiana native Why not? This is LSU football we're talking about here, with a head coach that has spent over $40 million on its roster this season. You bet that Kiffin and his staff felt the pressure in the week leading up to this one, and rightfully so. This was a game in which both teams could not afford to lose, even though that swayed more in the direction of LSU given their three losses. As day turned into night, the craziness began for both teams. Multiple interceptions, special teams blunders and some interesting play calling on each side of the field. But, it was Arch Manning that had the ball with just over two minutes remaining in a game that set offenses back years up until the final drive of the game. If there’s one thing we’ve learned about the Texas Longhorns this season, it’s that we can’t put anything past them. A 12-play, 58-yard drive would seal the deal for a Texas team that had one last chance to pull off a miracle in Baton Rouge. Were you expecting anything different? SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Arch Manning hit Raleek Brown on a swing pass that caught the LSU defense off guard, and Brown fought his way into the end zone to secure Texas’ 22-21 win, drawing a roar from a Texas crowd that had essentially taken over the southern end of Tiger Stadium. Just when you thought the Longhorns were done, the defense gave this team one last chance to pull off what many will remember as one of the best moments of Arch Manning's college career. Let me be clear that this Texas offense looked putrid at times, getting torched along the line of scrimmage, while Manning would end the game with three interceptions. But, all it took was one legendary drive for a quarterback that will be remembered for a number of inconsistencies in college. Arch Manning delivers at the most important time, ends the Tigers On Saturday night, none of that mattered when Manning grabbed Steve Sarkisian during the post-game interview with ESPN. His interceptions will be remembered by those who cover him on a daily basis, but the touchdown pass will live on forever in Texas lore. As Sarkisian and Manning headed towards the Texas end zone to greet the fans who made the chaotic trip to Baton Rouge, you could once again see what once again looked like disbelief come across the face of the starting quarterback. Not that Arch thought he couldn’t do it. But more so, the fact that so many things were not going his way leading up to that final drive. "Holy sh-t," Manning proclaimed as he bent over in the end zone during the postgame celebration. "That was incredible." On the other hand, LSU finds itself done with any talk of playing in the college football playoff. A roster worth over $40 million will now be sitting at home while others fight for a national championship, to the dismay of Tiger fans that bought into the words of their head coach. Fool you once, shame on you. Fool you four times, you're just out of luck. Arch Manning delivered a dagger to his home state on Saturday night, just when those around the college football community thought the Longhorns were done in Baton Rouge. We got the ending we deserved after sitting through that offensive disaster for nearly an entire game. For the Texas Longhorns, the season continues and a run towards the college football playoff might have started weeks ago. But tonight inside Tiger Stadium, Arch Manning and Steve Sarkisian dialed up a drive that will be remembered forever in Austin. And, it was the Tigers that brought out another side of a Manning that we have not seen before. Texas' season will more than likely continue into late December. articles.title: Francophone summit opens in Cambodia amid Rwanda-DR Congo rift
articles.summary: Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda clash over who should lead the organisation of French-speaking nations.
articles.body:
Leaders of the Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF) are meeting in Cambodia amid a dispute between the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Rwanda over who should lead the association of French-speaking nations, which threatens to split the group.

The OIF is holding a three-day summit in the Cambodian capital, Phnom Penh, through Monday. A loose confederation of 90 states and governments where French is spoken or widely used, the OIF has 53 full members, five associate members and 32 observers.

French President Emmanuel Macron, who chaired the last summit in 2024 and will hand the chair to Cambodia, arrived on Saturday and met Prime Minister Hun Manet, The Associated Press news agency reported.

About 20 leaders are expected, including Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, Vietnamese President To Lam, Rwandan President Paul Kagame and DRC President Felix Tshisekedi.

On Monday, leaders will choose the organisation’s next secretary-general for a four-year term.

Rwanda’s Louise Mushikiwabo, who has led the OIF since 2018, is seeking a third term.

The DRC, however, which accuses Rwanda of backing the M23 armed group in the country’s east, has threatened to leave the OIF if she is re-elected. Congo, the United States and United Nations experts say Rwanda backs the M23, one of about 100 armed groups in the mineral-rich region.

On Saturday, the DRC withdrew its candidate, Juliana Lumumba, the daughter of independence hero Patrice Lumumba, and backed Romanian former Prime Minister Dacian Ciolos to allow “consensus around a unifying candidacy”.

Rwanda’s foreign minister, Olivier Nduhungirehe, said Mushikiwabo would stay in the race. Mauritania’s Coumba Ba, a former minister, is also running, the AFP news agency reported.

Macron’s office said that most members agreed on the need for consensus and that he would take it up with his African counterparts. France is the biggest contributor to the OIF’s 2026 budget of 71.7 million euros ($79m).

Rwanda has said Macron asked Kagame to withdraw its candidate and that Kigali refused, AFP reported.

The DRC has a population of more than 110 million, roughly 40 million more than France, and is the most populous country where French is an official language. Its exit would be a blow to the organisation, which lost Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso, which announced their withdrawals in March 2025 following suspensions over military coups.

The summit’s slogan is “Reinvest in Peace for Shared Prosperity and Lasting Stability”. Activists see it as a chance to press Cambodia, a de facto one-party state, on rights.

UN Special Rapporteur Tom Andrews urged delegates to press for the release of detained activists. “No one should be detained for defending human rights, reporting on matters of public concern, or voicing critical opinions,” he said.

Macron arrived as France faces widespread protests at home. He is due to visit the Angkor World Heritage Site on Monday before leaving for Malaysia.

articles.title: South Korea’s viral ‘Scarf Man’ tells customers not to buy his products. They’re lining up anyway
articles.summary: A shopkeeper at Namdaemun Market in Seoul has become an anti-influencer thanks to his unorthodox sales strategy.
articles.body: Most shopkeepers will do just about anything to make a sale. But one merchant in Seoul has built an unexpected internet following by doing the exact opposite. “Didn’t you come here knowing that we sell nothing but crappy stuff?” he asks customers in a video shared on social media. “Didn’t you all come here to buy scarves for your doghouses?” Meet the Namdaemun Scarf Man. His unorthodox sales strategy is the opposite of the hard sell. Instead of talking about how great his products are, he tries to convince shoppers they don’t need a scarf at all. He complains about their requests, pokes fun at their shopping habits and occasionally suggests he might be better off quitting the business altogether. Maybe it’s reverse psychology. But it’s working. Hundreds of people have been flocking to his small shop inside Seoul’s sprawling Namdaemun Market for a chance to meet the man behind the viral videos. The international travelers joining the queue may not even be able to understand his Korean-language zingers, but that doesn’t stop them from showing up anyway. The scarves themselves are hardly a luxury purchase. Six sell for 10,000 won, or about $7. But it seems the merchandise isn’t the point. Historic market, modern-day fame Namdaemun is one of Seoul’s most recognizable traditional markets, a maze of hundreds of shops and stalls. Vendors of clothing, handbags, shoes, household goods and snacks all push up against each other, competing for space. For generations, it has been a place where merchants and customers haggle, bargain and build relationships face-to-face. Videos of Scarf Man’s colorful exchanges with customers have spread across social media, earning him more than 100,000 Instagram followers and a growing audience on YouTube. His online popularity has even translated into a new online store, where customers can purchase his scarves without making the trip to Seoul. The first batch of products sold out within 24 hours. Fittingly, Scarf Man has since asked customers to cancel their orders because he received too many. Still, plenty of fans would rather see the man in person. Some visitors have traveled considerable distances, only to find his shop closed or the day’s customers already turned away. It’s not just about the scarves Ahn Hyo-sun traveled across Seoul to visit the shop after repeatedly watching clips of Scarf Man online. She arrived hoping to meet him, but missed her chance. “I heard his voice earlier, so I got really excited thinking he must be here,” she said. The vendor’s humor provides a welcome pick-me-up. Followers compare his entertaining, occasionally foul-mouthed remarks to those of a hilarious grandmother. “Listening to this man’s funny banter gives them a kind of happiness boost,” she said. Another customer, Cho Yoon-sook, traveled roughly an hour and a half from Incheon, west of Seoul, hoping to catch a glimpse of him. She had already been turned away once after arriving too late. “Maybe I’ll come back tomorrow,” she said. “I’ve made up my mind to come all this way, so I have to see him at least once.” Cho said she wasn’t particularly interested in the scarves — just in the Scarf Man. “There’s something endearing about the way he talks,” she said. A man of mystery For all the attention surrounding him, there’s still plenty about Scarf Man that remains unknown — like his name. In a livestream on social media he shared that he’s married with children and has been selling various products at Namdaemun for years, but that’s about all we know. Even figuring out when his shop will be open has become something of a guessing game. CNN tried visiting three days in a row this week, and only on the last day did we briefly catch Scarf Man as he closed up his store. As he did so, people watched in awe, with their cameras out, cheering when he turned and gave a quick smile. These days, it seems like everyone is chasing viral fame, or eager to embrace it if it comes along. In Italy, Venetian Monica Poli became a social media sensation after she took it upon herself to warn tourists when they were about to be pickpocketed. Poli’s Attenzione, pickpocket! warning became an oft-shared earworm online, and she told CNN that she appreciated being thanked for the work she calls her “mission.” Meanwhile, a good-looking Istanbul native named Alper Temel became a viral celebrity while selling corn and chestnuts at a roadside stall with his brothers. Online fans dubbed him the “corn star” and began flocking to the stall to get selfies. Temel has taken the attention in stride, and the family business is booming. But Scarf Man doesn’t seem to be chasing the influencer dream. He has turned down myriad interview requests, including from CNN. In an age where social media can turn just about anyone into a celebrity, this merchant has found an odd but effective way to stand out: telling people his products aren’t worth buying. Judging by the lines outside his shop, customers aren’t listening.

articles.title: Secret votes and vetoes: How will the next UN chief be picked?
articles.summary: With no frontrunner for the job, eight candidates are vying for the UN Security Council’s recommendation.
articles.body:
Secret votes, coloured ballot papers, straw polls and backroom efforts to force a consensus — with the threat of powerful vetoes hanging over it all. These could be the contours of how boards of multibillion-dollar corporations decide on contentious issues.

It is also the way the United Nations picks its secretary-general, the person at the apex of a vast and sprawling machinery tasked with upholding fast-fraying international laws and practices.

That process is now barrelling towards a tense climax, with the UN Security Council (UNSC) holding multiple straw polls in a bid to select its new secretary-general by December 31, when incumbent Antonio Guterres must step down.

Eight candidates are in the fray — from Costa Rica’s Rebeca Grynspan, the head of the UN Conference on Trade and Development, the organisation’s trade body, and Rafael Grossi, the Argentinian head of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), to Lana Nusseibeh, the United Arab Emirates minister of state for foreign affairs.

The UNSC recommends a candidate who gets nine votes without a veto from its five permanent members. The process ends after the UN General Assembly (UNGA) gives its seal of approval to that candidate.

In effect, the 15-member UNSC chooses the UN chief.

The council has five permanent members – China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States – who hold veto power.

In addition, there are 10 nonpermanent members, elected every two years, who make up the council. Bahrain, Colombia, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Denmark, Greece, Latvia, Liberia, Pakistan, Panama and Somalia are the current UNSC members.

According to Article 97 of the UN Charter, the UNSC decides on a candidate and recommends them to the UNGA for a vote by all members.

There has never been a time when the council has picked a candidate who was voted down by the assembly, meaning that while, in theory, everyone has a say, the UNGA has never gone against the UNSC. And because the five permanent members wield a veto, the secretary-general is, in effect, chosen by them, once they have convinced the nonpermanent members.

However, in 1950, the UNGA voted to extend the term of the then secretary-general without the UNSC’s recommendation after a deadlock in the council.

The council holds informal, anonymous polls, also known as straw polls, on whether the members “encourage”, “discourage”, or “have no opinion” about a candidate.

Although it is expected to be secret, the number of encourage, discourage, or no-opinion votes is often leaked.

In later rounds of voting, coloured paper ballots are used to distinguish between the UNSC’s permanent and nonpermanent members, providing a clearer sense of their leanings.

Once a straw poll confirms that a candidate has at least nine “encourage” votes and no vetoes against them, the council holds a formal vote to recommend them to the UNGA, which is expected to endorse that nomination.

Jane Kinninmont, CEO of UN Association-UK, an independent, nongovernmental organisation, explained that the process to select a candidate has traditionally been “closed and secretive” but has become more open as a result of campaigning by civil society groups and member states.

“However, the Security Council continues to guard its secrecy tightly – part of a political culture that many other countries regard as outmoded,” Kinninmont told Al Jazeera.

“One of the stated reasons is that no country wants to have a situation where it votes for one candidate, but another candidate actually is appointed and resents them for not voting for them,” she said.

Al Jazeera’s UN correspondent, Gabriel Elizondo, also explained that the secrecy behind the selection was just due to the way the system was set up.

“Now, there have been some talks in recent years, including this year, about trying to make the process more transparent in the Security Council, but the five permanent members just want to keep it the way that it is,” he said.

Eight people are running to become secretary-general after some candidates dropped out earlier in the race.

Two leading candidates are IAEA chief Grossi and UNCTAD head Grynspan.

Grynspan, who, if successful, could become the first woman and first Jewish person to lead the UN, played a key role in brokering the Black Sea Grain Initiative between Russia and Ukraine in 2022. The deal allowed for millions of tonnes of food to be exported from war-torn Ukraine, much of which went to developing nations.

Grossi has headed the IAEA since 2019 and has been at the centre of the UN’s efforts to prevent nuclear escalations between Russia and Ukraine amid their ongoing war. But Grossi has also faced criticism, especially from Iran, over perceptions that some of his reports critiquing its nuclear programme helped provide a pretext for the US and Israel to attack Iran.

Maria Fernanda Espinosa Garces (former UNGA chief, Ecuador)

Feridun Hadi Sinirlioglu ( chief of Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe, Turkiye)

Carolyn Rodrigues Birkett (Guyana’s ambassador to the UN)

What’s happened in the 2026 straw polls so far?

Eight polls have been held so far, but no consensus has emerged on a candidate who has received no “discourage” votes.

According to the 1 for 8 Billion campaign, supported by organisations and individuals worldwide to call for a fair, open and inclusive selection process for the UN chief’s job, Grynspan led the eighth poll.

Last week’s poll saw Grynspan receive 12 encourage votes and three discourage votes. In second place, Grossi received nine encourage votes, four discourage votes and two no-opinion votes. He was followed by Birkett, who received eight encourage votes, five discourage votes and two no-opinion votes.

While it is unclear how the permanent members voted and whether any had used a veto, candidates need zero discourage votes from them to secure the nomination.

According to Kinninmont, there is “growing resentment” about the permanent UNSC members using their vetoes that have often led to a paralysed council.

“The appointment of the SG is a different issue from any single conflict, but ultimately this person is supposed to be the world’s leading defender of the UN Charter and a spokesperson for the peoples of the world, in whose name the charter is written,” she said.

“Thus, it seems hard to defend the idea that any single power should be able to veto a candidate even if that candidate has the support of the majority of other countries on the Security Council and indeed a majority of the countries in the world.”

On more powers for the UNGA in the selection process, Elizondo said while there is talk of reforming the system, it would mean the permanent members would have to give up some of their power.

“None of them wants to give up their power because, essentially, the truth is, while the United Nations is made up of 193 member states, it’s really the five permanent members that really have the overwhelming amount of power to select who the next secretary-general is,” he said.

What happens if no one is picked by December 31?

There is nothing in the UN Charter about what happens if no candidate is picked before Guterres’s term ends.

The UNSC has some options if it is struggling to decide on a pick, including recommending a candidate for a shorter term or compromising on a candidate, as it did in 1996 to select Kofi Annan after a deadlock.

Member states could also let a senior UN official oversee operations in the meantime.

According to Elizondo, Guterres has also been asked whether he would stay on if no secretary-general was selected.

“He gives a pretty noncommittal answer. He says as of January 1, he hopes to be and expects to be back home in Portugal. What would happen? Nobody knows because that’s never happened before,” Elizondo said.

Kinninmont said one way of achieving a more “transparent and democratic process” in selecting a candidate could be for the UNSC to agree on two or three candidates and the UNGA to vote on those.

articles.title: Mental health: It's no joke - but I've turned it into a stand-up routine
articles.summary: People who have struggled with mental ill-health are giving stand-up a go to tell their stories.
articles.body:
Stepping onto the stage for the first time, Michael Hart is "flying" with adrenaline.

He didn't think he had it in him, but he's about to tell his own jokes to a room full of strangers.

He stutters at first but soon gets his first laugh from the crowd and the nerves he's feeling are washed away by a wave of elation.

Michael is part of a group of people who have struggled with mental ill-health and are now giving stand-up a go to build up their self-belief and connect with others.

Through the Finding Our Funny workshops run by the charity Inspire, they're turning their experiences into comedy material - and then taking it on the road for three gigs across Northern Ireland this month.

Michael has sought help for his mental health over the past few years and has struggled with his confidence.

Given those circumstances, throwing himself into stand-up is a daunting prospect - but he's embraced the challenge.

"The first thing I said was: 'What's the worst that can go wrong?

"I did stutter at the start, I sort of froze - but I came back in again. Just a joy to get up there. I think I kept it together well.

"My wee trick was I done a lot of practising."

He's now performed three gigs, using all his own material.

"It's all true, I didn't make any of this stuff up."

Carla Sloan says she's had mental health issues for most of her adult life and had never imagined trying her hand at stand-up until now.

"I've done lots of mental health courses on emotional resilience and stuff but this was something completely different.

"The first day I drove into the car park and then I was like: 'No.'

"I turned the car around and I drove back down the road and then I thought: 'Ah, I'm here, I might as well go in and see what it's about'."

As a mum of teenagers, Carla's jokes are about her real-life experiences of parenting.

"All my material is based on teenage girls and the fun you have raising them but also when they do something that they aren't meant to do," she smiles.

Tim McGarry is a veteran of the Northern Ireland comedy scene, best known for playing Da in the long-running BBC sitcom Give My Head Peace.

For decades he's given audiences the giggles with his own stand-up shows, so who better to mentor this bunch of budding comics?

For McGarry, the approach to comedy should be a simple one.

"I just sat down with them and said, well, what makes you laugh? What's something funny in your life?

"Most of them went off and wrote stuff themselves and I tweaked a bit and helped a wee bit - but it's coming from entirely the participants themselves."

While some comic techniques can be taught, McGarry says, much of his work as a mentor involved building their self-belief.

Getting "out of their comfort zone" and taking that first step onto the stage is the hard part, says McGarry - but the payoff is worth it.

"There is no better feeling than coming off stage and going: 'You know what? I made people laugh'."

"When I looked back at my videos I couldn't believe how well I'd done. My family is very proud of me," he says.

"My goal is to get back into work - and this has raised my confidence even more."

The experience has given Carla a fresh belief in herself too.

"I've learnt not to underestimate myself - and that was a big one for me as I do tend to underestimate what I'm capable of.

"Maybe I need to look at myself a bit more and be aware of just how much I can do.

"I might have to take things slower than other people - but I can still do it."

Inspire chief executive Kerry Anthony says the project is something very different to what the charity would normally do.

Much of its work involves helping people who are dealing with mental ill-health, homelessness or addiction - but Kerry says that talking about those "heavy" topics through humour has been "wonderful" for those in the stand-up workshops.

"People who use our services... have worked with us over the years to use their voice around very serious issues to do with mental ill-health.

"This was a time that they could use their voice in a totally different way.

"Comedy isn't a treatment for mental ill health - but comedy is important for everybody."

articles.title: US-Iran war: IRGC targets American air defence radar at Bahrain base with six drones, warns of retaliation
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) on Sunday claimed that it had targeted a US air defence radar installation at Bahrain's
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) on Sunday claimed that it had targeted a US air defence radar installation at Bahrain's Al-Rifaa helicopter base with six drones, warning that any further US aggression would invite a stronger response.In a statement released on Sunday morning, the IRGC said its Aerospace Force carried out the attack as part of what it described as the second phase of its response to US military actions. The claim has not been independently verified, and there was no immediate confirmation from US or Bahraini authorities of damage to the radar installation.“The precise and successful impact of these drones was heard in various parts of Bahrain, once again demonstrating the IRGC’s operational capabilities,” the statement said.The IRGC described the operation as the “second phase of a decisive and crushing response to [US] aggression” and claimed that it had deployed more drones against American targets than during the previous phase.The Iranian force also accused Washington of attempting to divert international attention from the closure of the Strait of Hormuz through what it called limited and indiscriminate military actions.“However, the IRGC’s elite young officers once again declare loudly: The Strait of Hormuz is closed, and any aggression by the American enemy will be met with a harsher and more crushing response,” it added.The statement further warned that every act of aggression would invite a “tough” and “calculated” response.Bahrain issues security alerts amid Iranian claimsBahrain's Interior Ministry issued two alerts warning residents of potential threats on Sunday, urging people to remain calm and move to safe locations. The alerts were the first of their kind since September, according to Reuters.The latest Iranian claim follows another reported attack on a US early-warning radar installation in Bahrain on Friday. The IRGC had then claimed that its Aerospace Force destroyed the radar in a precision strike.However, the US Central Command (CENTCOM) rejected the claim, saying American forces had intercepted two Iranian drones heading towards Bahrain and that there were no casualties or damage.The IRGC had described the earlier operation as “a serious warning to the aggressor enemy to cease its aerial provocations and oil smuggling in the Strait of Hormuz.”Strait of Hormuz remains key flashpointThe latest developments come amid the ongoing conflict involving Iran, the United States and Israel, which began on February 28. The conflict has expanded across West Asia, with Iranian forces targeting US military assets and infrastructure in the Gulf region.Iran has repeatedly warned against attempts to challenge its control over maritime movement through the Strait of Hormuz, a critical international shipping route connecting the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman.The waterway has become a major point of contention between Tehran and Washington, with restrictions on shipping raising concerns over global energy supplies and maritime security.You use AI every day. articles.title: ASEAN summit: Who’s attending and what’s at stake?
articles.summary: Energy disruptions as a result of the US-Israel war on Iran is a key issue for the import-dependent bloc.
articles.body:
Southeast Asian countries that comprise the ASEAN economic bloc will meet in the Philippines this week as the region continues to bear the brunt of oil shortages caused by the US-Israel war on Iran, as well as by US-China rivalry, which has hit economies hard.

The Manila summit will be held from November 15 to 17 and will include US President Donald Trump and several other world leaders.

The 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) aims to establish a single market, although it cannot impose decisions on members. It comprises Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Brunei, Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, Cambodia and East Timor, with a combined population of nearly 694 million, or 8.4 percent of the world’s population.

Several ASEAN meetings are held annually. This week’s summit is expected to be the final one for this year.

Beyond the energy crisis, other pressing issues include disputes over the South China Sea and trade.

In addition to leaders and representatives from the 11 member countries, other guests include:

US President Donald Trump – Trump is expected to hold a special summit with ASEAN members on November 17 as Washington’s trade tensions with China continue. He is also set to hold a one-on-one meeting with Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. Afterwards, Trump is due to head to China for the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting on 18-19 November.

India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi – Although India is not part of ASEAN, India is a key trading partner to member states.

Canada’s Prime Minister Mark Carney – Carney is set to give a speech at the summit.

Brazil’s President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva – His visit will be the first by a sitting Brazilian president to the Philippines. He is expected to discuss trade, defence and other areas of cooperation with ASEAN members.

Russia Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov – His visit comes after the Russia-ASEAN summit in July.

The summit is being held at a time when Southeast Asian countries have been hit hard by shortages in oil and gas supplies from Middle Eastern suppliers amid the US-Israel war on Iran.

The Philippines, Vietnam and Malaysia are among the most vulnerable to the energy disruptions in the Gulf, with Manila declaring a state of national energy emergency in March.

Millions of ASEAN citizens also live and work in the Middle East, where the war threatens their safety and earnings.

Meanwhile, Asian countries are worried the conflict could spill into the Strait of Malacca, a narrow waterway between Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore.

The US’s tariff war has seen ASEAN countries slapped with 10-12.5 percent tariff hikes since the beginning of US President Donald Trump’s second term in the White House, prompting the bloc to strengthen trade relationships elsewhere.

China and four ASEAN members – Brunei, Malaysia, the Philippines and Vietnam – as well as Taiwan, have been locked in decades of territorial standoffs in the busy waterway.

The area is important as it is believed to host undersea deposits of oil and gas.

In 2005, the bloc began negotiating a “code of conduct” with China to discourage aggression and prevent major clashes. The negotiations have often stalled, however, partly due to flared tensions, especially between Manila and Beijing in recent years.

In 2023, the two sides agreed to speed things up and release a finished draft this year. At least 10 rounds of talks have been held this year, led by Malaysia, with a final round taking place in October.

However, analysts doubt a definite conclusion will be reached at the summit this week, meaning talks could continue into next year.

Armed clashes broke out between the two ASEAN member states late last year along an 800km (500-mile) contested border area, as well as over competing claims to sacred religious sites, such as the Preah Vihear Shiva temple.

At least 150 people were reported to have been killed, and nearly one million displaced.

ASEAN members, as well as China and the US, intervened, leading to talks. Although a ceasefire has been in place since December, the wider border dispute remains unresolved, and the bloc is calling for more dialogue and the participation of third-party observers.

The ongoing civil war in Myanmar, which has compounded the Rohingya refugee crisis , has been at the top of the agenda as the bloc pushes for the restoration of democracy in the country.

Multiple rebel forces, some of them ethnic-based armed groups, have been fighting the military government since the country’s February 2021 coup.

ASEAN has already restricted Myanmar’s participation at important summits to non-political representatives as concerns about violence and a humanitarian crisis grow.

The bloc’s five-point Myanmar peace plan, launched in April 2021 and calling for dialogue and improved humanitarian aid access, has meanwhile failed to alleviate the situation.

Months of widespread wildfires in drought-hit Indonesia have scorched an estimated 2.88 million hectares (7.12 million acres) and resulted in at least 3,500 deaths.

The resulting haze has severely impacted not just the country’s residents, but also those in neighbouring Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and East Timor.

Jakarta has faced criticism for failing to effectively respond to the fires, but the government has defended its approach, saying thousands of responders have been deployed.

articles.title: Weekly round-up: Five stories you may have missed
articles.summary: Queen Mary 2's 450th crossing and a wedding-crashing dog feature in our most-read stories this week.
articles.body:
A four-legged gatecrasher and a milestone for the only remaining transatlantic liner all feature among the most-popular stories in the south of England this week.

In case you missed them, we have picked five articles from the past seven days across Hampshire, the Isle of Wight, Dorset, Berkshire and Oxfordshire to keep you up to date.

'Five years of Long Covid and my symptoms are worse'

As 18-year-old Molly Foden walks along the beach near her home, she explains what it has been like living with Long Covid for five years.

"I get a lot of dizziness, I'm very fatigued, and I have a lot of body weakness and pain," she says.

There are no official figures for the number living with the condition but the charity Long Covid Kids estimate it affects thousands of children and says it has supported 11,000 families during the past six years.

Molly , from Weymouth, Dorset, says she has learnt to live with the symptoms.

"I've had a lot of stomach trouble, food not digesting, a lot of sickness and pain which meant I was in hospital for two months plus," she said.

"No one knew what to do with me, no one knew what was wrong. It was really hard."

Dog gatecrashes wedding as bride and groom watch on

A newly married couple have described the "hilarious" moment when a runaway dog gatecrashed their wedding .

Simon and Amy Keane's wedding was about to begin on Saturday afternoon when a passing Jack Russell sprinted into the church in Eastleigh, Hampshire.

It then ran around members of the congregation and joined the couple's own dog, Duggie, who was due to be a ring bearer.

Simon, 31, who had been feeling nervous as he waited for his bride's big entrance, said it had been "kind of hilarious".

Asylum centre on military base near Piddington approved

Plans to house asylum seekers at a former military site near the Oxfordshire village of Piddington have been approved by the government .

Planning permission for housing for up to 1,256 men at the MoD Bicester site was approved by the Housing Secretary Angela Rayner after the Home Office used a fast-track route for projects deemed to be urgently needed and of national importance.

The Home Office said this would allow it to continue developing the plan but that no final decision on the site had been taken.

Piddington symbolically voted to leave the UK over the planned use for the site, which has also been legally challenged by campaigners. Opponents now have six weeks to challenge the approval.

Hungry squirrel trapped in bird feeder rescued

An unfortunate squirrel who became stuck in a bird feeder was freed after firefighters came to its aid.

The animal was found wedged inside the device in a garden in Byron Road, Earley, at about 09:00 GMT on 4 November.

Royal Berkshire Fire and Rescue Service said a crew from Wokingham Road fire station "came to the rescue" of the "rather unlucky" rodent.

It said: "Equipped with wire cutters, the crew were on hand to safely rescue the furry friend before releasing it back into the wild."

The only remaining transatlantic liner, Queen Mary 2, has reached a milestone with its 450th crossing.

The record-breaking vessel left Southampton on Tuesday on the seven-day voyage to New York.

The Cunard flagship is an echo of the golden age of transatlantic liners from the early part of the 20th Century.

articles.title: UPS cargo plane, Copa Airlines passenger jet collide at Miami airport, leaving 2 injured
articles.summary: A UPS Airlines cargo plane and a Copa Airlines passenger jet collided on the ground at Miami International Airport on Saturday night, leaving two people with minor injuries.
articles.body: A UPS cargo plane and a Copa Airlines passenger jet collided on the ground at Miami International Airport Saturday night, leaving two people with minor injuries, airport officials confirmed. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said the wingtip of a Copa Airlines Boeing 737 struck the nose of a UPS Boeing 767 while both aircraft were taxiing around 9 p.m. local time. Air traffic controllers had instructed the UPS crew to give way to the Copa Airlines flight, which was heading to its gate after landing, while the UPS cargo plane was preparing to depart for Bogotá, Colombia, according to the FAA. The agency said it is investigating the collision. AMAZON CARGO PLANE OVERRUNS MIAMI AIRPORT RUNWAY AND STRIKES 'MULTIPLE' VEHICLES; 5 DEAD, 5 INJURED "At approximately 9:15 p.m., an arriving aircraft and a departing aircraft made contact with each other at the intersection of two taxiways," Greg Chin, communications director for the Miami-Dade Aviation Department, said in a statement. "Flights are being directed to other taxiways, so there is no impact to airport operations at this time. Two patients were treated on the scene by Miami-Dade Fire Rescue for minor injuries and did not require medical transport," Chin added. Air traffic control audio reviewed by Fox News Digital captured an exchange between pilots and a controller following the collision. A pilot aboard the Copa Airlines flight was heard saying, "Somebody just hit us." NTSB REPORT DETAILS HOW CONTROLLER DECISION AND TECH FAILURES LED TO DEADLY RUNWAY COLLISION "UPS 358, did you hit that aircraft?" an air traffic controller asked. "Yeah, we went too far and he clipped us with his wing," the UPS pilot responded. Copa Airlines said Flight CM427, arriving from Panama City, Panama, was carrying 166 passengers and six crew members when the collision occurred. The airline said the Boeing 737's left wingtip was involved in the collision with the cargo plane while both aircraft were taxiing. All passengers disembarked at the terminal, with two receiving treatment for apparent minor injuries, the airline added. UPS Airlines also acknowledged the incident in a statement posted on X. "We are aware of an incident involving one of our aircraft on the ground in Miami," the company said. 4 CRITICAL TRAVEL ISSUES FOR THOSE DELAYED AND DISRUPTED BY FAA NATIONWIDE GROUND STOP "Our crew is safe, and we are committed to working with authorities to determine what happened. The safety of our employees and the public is our highest priority." The collision came as U.S. airports continued recovering from Friday's nationwide Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ground stop, which disrupted thousands of flights after radar and communications systems experienced instability. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Saturday that air traffic control communications had returned to full operations, while FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said airlines expected to restore their full schedules by the end of Sunday.
